---
title: "Ping reference dapp"
description: "Modular local monitoring, delegated application checkpoints and native FILE history on a private Riadchain network."
---

Ping combines local connectivity checks, explicit device discovery, decoy metadata
and phone alerts with recoverable chain records. Its version-2 source lives in
`dapps/Ping/`. It illustrates an application
runtime with narrowly delegated publication; it is not another consensus engine
or a proof that measurements are truthful.

## Local monitoring and immediate alerts

One monitoring host runs independent, bounded programs:

| Program | Observations |
| --- | --- |
| Connectivity | Configured ICMP, DNS and HTTPS checks, normally every 15 seconds |
| Discovery | Host responses on explicitly authorized private subnets |
| Decoys | Whitelisted SSH/HTTP interaction metadata, excluding attempted credentials |
| Notifications | Durable ntfy publishing attempts and service acceptance |

The monitor atomically saves its current snapshot, cursors and contiguous
observation journal in SQLite. Detailed monitoring records are **plaintext** for
private deployments. Keys, RPC tokens, raw decoy logs and attempted credentials
must not enter the journal, dashboard assets or native FILE archives.

Local incidents and ntfy attempts continue when the chain or publisher is
unavailable. Service acceptance does not establish phone delivery. Discovery does
not authenticate devices; an unfamiliar address is not proof of intrusion. Ping
performs no packet capture, general flow analysis or automatic firewall blocking.

## Two-minute checkpoints and FILE history

A separate publisher submits selected current state approximately every two
minutes. The contract checks its configured publisher, configuration epoch,
contiguous record range and previous commitment. Typed hashes bind the payload
to the authenticated chain, genesis and contract identity. Snapshot-pinned reads
provide a consistent contract view while preparing a submission.

The contract keeps compact current metadata and checkpoint/archive heads rather
than duplicating the entire observation history in active state. Acceptance emits
`CheckpointAccepted`; confirmed FILE references emit `ArchivePublished`. These are
application records, separate from a node's derived persistence checkpoints.

Detailed observations become deterministic gzip JSON Lines archives in **native
FILE storage**. A window seals when its oldest record is about fifteen minutes
old or a full 1,000-record part is ready. Bounded parts drain consecutively after
matching receipts; a recent short tail waits. Each archive is limited to 4 MiB
compressed and 32 MiB expanded. The publisher confirms the original FILE upload
and verifies CID/size before publishing its contract reference.

Retrieve bytes with the SDK and use `checkpoints/archive.ts` to verify scope,
hashes, ranges and bounded decoding. Checkpoints recover selected state; confirmed
FILE archives recover detailed observations. A CID or receipt alone does not prove
that a node currently has the bytes. Newer unpublished records remain local.
History still grows on disk; see [contract resource practices](/build/resource-practices/).

## Administration and limited publication

Deployment pins the bootstrap account and initial admin NFT recipient before
compilation. Initialization cannot be claimed by an arbitrary first caller.
The current NFT holder controls publisher selection, publication pause and program
settings. Existing contract administration does not grant chain governance.

The publisher receives a native capability scoped to one contract and the methods
`acceptCheckpoint`, `publishArchive` and `FILE`. It has finite fee escrow, FILE
allowance, a height expiry and at most one call per block. It receives no owner
spending key. Expiry, revocation or insufficient resources prevent new publication;
funding is manual. Dashboard reviews distinguish fee top-ups from FILE allowance
and expiry, and require the appropriate wallet signature.

The authenticated dashboard uses admin NFT ownership. Its monitor holds no node
RPC credential or signing key; chain reads use the publisher's restricted read
relay. Keep the publisher key, node bearer credential and relay token in separate
protected server-side files. These files are plaintext custody protected by local
permissions, not encrypted backups.

Every signed original and FILE payload is retained before a broadcast-capable
operation. Lost responses remain unresolved. Reconcile the original receipt;
timeout or wall-clock age does not authorize a replacement. See
[transaction outcomes and recovery](/developers/transactions/).

## Run an isolated reference

Install the [monorepo dependencies](/developers/sdk/#develop-in-the-monorepo)
and use a current native binary with
the [funded regtest launcher](/node/regtest/):

```sh
bun run regtest:start
bun dapps/Ping/scripts/deploy.ts --config "$PWD/.tmp/regtest/deployment.json"
bun dapps/Ping/scripts/deploy.ts --config "$PWD/.tmp/regtest/deployment.json" --apply
```

The launcher produces a genesis-pinned version-2 deployment input with explicit
admin, fee and FILE limits. The plan command prepares local identities and its
journal without broadcasting. `--apply` spends disposable regtest funds and writes
a manifest only after matching successful execution receipts.

See the [Ping README](https://github.com/nfl0/riadchain/blob/master/dapps/Ping/README.md)
for builds, configuration and qualification. Historical private deployment records
from October 21–22, 2026 describe an earlier revision; this v2 source guide does
not establish that those services have been replaced. A live installation requires
its own authorized deployment, protected configuration, verified cutover and admin
NFT handover. No universal live contract address is supplied.
